channel.title: Nordic Crypto
channel.description: ناروے، سویڈن، ڈنمارک، فن لینڈ اور آئس لینڈ سے بٹ کوائن، بلاک چین اور کرپٹو کی خبریں، انگریزی خلاصوں، تقریبات کے کیلنڈر اور “کون کیا ہے” کے ساتھ۔

item.title: Bitcoin presses av rekordstore uttak
item.description: Exchange-traded bitcoin products saw net outflows of 10,064 bitcoin in five days, the largest since 15 September, as bitcoin fell from USD 86,000 to below USD 80,500, according to K33's weekly report as covered by Investornytt. K33's head of analysis attributes the fall mainly to a broader flight from risk. According to K33's weekly report, open positions in perpetual futures are at a five-month low, which makes forced liquidations unlikely, and K33 still considers bitcoin attractively priced with limited downside.

item.title: Frankrike vill beskatta kryptomiljonärer som flyttar utomlands
item.description: Realtid reports, citing Euronews and Journal du Coin, that the French National Assembly's finance committee voted to extend the country's exit tax to crypto assets above EUR 800,000 from 2027, and backed fines of up to EUR 10,000 for undeclared self-custody wallets worth EUR 100,000 or more. The proposals are not yet law and may still fall.

item.title: Bred enighed om ny kryptoskat: Forslaget har ligget i skuffen i over et år
item.description: Børsen reports that a broad working group of authorities, business and the crypto industry agreed on a new crypto tax model more than a year ago, but the proposal has since been shelved. The government is now signalling new rules.

item.title: Amerikansk finanspresse oppdager at tokenisering endrer børs og aksjehandel
item.description: Kaupr summarises recent US financial press coverage, saying Barron's, the Wall Street Journal, CNBC and Bloomberg all wrote about stock tokenisation in early October. According to that coverage, tokenised shares could bring round-the-clock trading and faster settlement, and an ICE–OKX venture is preparing to tokenise stocks.

item.title: Krypto i Kautokeino: – Kommunen vært naiv
item.description: In a follow-up to its earlier report that data-centre firm Arctic Core admits to 'a little' crypto mining on its site in Kautokeino, Ságat reports that the local Naturvernforbundet branch wants the municipality to withdraw the building permit. The group's complaint will not be handled before November, when it may be passed to the county governor.

item.title: Manipulation: Kryptoplånböcker tömdes på 860 miljoner
item.description: Dagens PS reports, citing The Verge, that a suspected supply-chain attack using a hidden circuit board in some Ledger hardware wallets may have let an attacker capture recovery phrases and drain accounts, with losses estimated at about USD 86 million. Ledger has confirmed an unauthorised hardware component in one affected user's device and asked the reseller involved to pause sales during an investigation.

item.title: Spillpioner og kapitalforvalter satser sammen på tokenisering
item.description: Kaupr reports, based on the companies' announcement at TOKEN2049 in Singapore, that games and Web3 company Animoca Brands and asset manager Franklin Templeton have entered a strategic partnership around NUVA, Animoca's marketplace for tokenised assets. According to the companies, they have also launched a four-part research series on tokenisation.

item.title: Aksjer på blokkjeden kan forsterke børsuro
item.description: Investornytt reports that an IMF financial-stability chapter on tokenisation found price swings in its sample of tokenised stock products about 50 percent larger than in traditional markets, with notably weaker liquidity. The IMF warns that automatic forced sales could amplify market stress as the market grows.

item.title: AI kan tømme lommebøkene
item.description: Investornytt reports that Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake believes AI could help break ECDSA, the signature scheme behind Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets, in the worst case within months, and suggests moving funds to addresses whose public key has not been exposed. Vitalik Buterin calls the risk serious but warns against panic.

item.title: Eksperimenterer med den norske kronen i internasjonal sandkasse
item.description: FinFacts has interviewed DNB about its experiments with the Norwegian krone in an international sandbox for tokenised bank deposits. According to the article's lead, DNB believes tokenised bank deposits will play at least as important a role as stablecoins in shaping the digital money of the future. The full interview is behind a paywall.

item.title: Innrømmer «litt» kryptoutvinning
item.description: Data-centre company Arctic Core now acknowledges that it will carry out 'a little' crypto mining in Kautokeino, the local paper Ságat reports. In writing, the company argues that using crypto mining to generate income during a test phase does not change the basic character of the warehouse building it has been granted a permit for. According to Ságat, the building is mainly meant for testing and storing equipment.

item.title: 30 nya namn på varningslistan – akta dig för företagen
item.description: Sweden's Finansinspektionen has warned against 30 more firms that look legitimate but lack a licence; several lure consumers with trading in shares, crypto and currencies, and some are clone firms using details of real financial companies. FI has now warned against 227 suspected investment-fraud operators so far in 2026 and urges people to check its company register before sending money.

item.title: Amla föreslår tre tekniska standarder enligt penningtvättsförordningen
item.description: The EU anti-money-laundering authority AMLA has sent three final draft technical standards under the new AML regulation to the European Commission, Sweden's Finansinspektionen reports; they still need the Commission's adoption. Under AMLA's report, crypto-asset service providers must consider whether a customer has made three or more transactions in 12 months when deciding if there is a business relationship, use a one-month window for linked transactions, and keep the €1,000 threshold for occasional transactions.

item.title: Småsparere hamstret krypto under renteuro
item.description: Customers of Norwegian exchange Firi bought 16.1 million kroner more crypto than they sold in September, on trading of 313.5 million kroner, despite a turbulent month. Bitcoin was the top buy while many moved money out of XRP into bitcoin and solana; CEO Thuc Hoang sees rising US interest rates as the main risk.

item.title: Rødt foreslår midlertidig stans for nye datasentre
item.description: The Red Party (Rødt) has proposed in the Storting a temporary halt for new data centres, along with a licensing regime and other measures. Its reasoning says crypto-mining data centres get power ahead of key local industries and that the crypto-mining ban the Storting has asked for three times in two years is still not in place, though none of the proposals singles out crypto.

item.title: Ace Digital tjente 6,3 millioner kroner i tredje kvartal
item.description: Ace Digital, listed on Euronext Growth Oslo, reported an unaudited third-quarter net profit of NOK 6.32 million, with equity up 19.3% to NOK 39.09 million and debt reduced to zero. The company says the value of its bitcoin treasury rose 373% without buying bitcoin, and estimates its economic exposure at about 57 BTC.

item.title: Representantforslag om konsesjonssystem for etablering av datasentre
item.description: Socialist Left Party (SV) MPs have proposed in the Storting a «panic law» that would put new data centres on hold until the industry is regulated, plus a national licensing system for data centres. They also ask the government to report back quickly on how the Storting's decision to ban crypto mining in Norway will be followed up; this is a proposal, not a decision.

item.title: Så kan Sverige användas för att finansiera kärnvapen
item.description: Crypto-assets and illegal financial networks are the biggest risks for UN sanctions against Iran and North Korea being evaded via Sweden, according to a new national risk assessment by ten Swedish authorities, Realtid reports. The authorities say organised crime has built an illegal financial infrastructure for cash, gold and conversion into crypto that could also be used for such financing. Realtid also notes that no one has been convicted of sanctions offences in Sweden in five years.

item.title: Uppgifter: Tonåringar silvertejpade man i jakt på kryptovaluta
item.description: Three teenagers, two aged 19 and one aged 16, have been arrested in Lund on suspicion of kidnapping and aggravated weapons offences, Sydsvenskan reports. According to information obtained by the newspaper, they had taken on a job to rob a local man of cryptocurrency and bound him with duct tape. Police have said little about the details and initially described the incident as a disturbance in a flat.

item.title: Tiltalt for dopsalg mot kryptovaluta på det mørke nettet
item.description: Three Norwegians and a Swede have been charged in a large drug case with links abroad, the Southern Norway public prosecutor's office says, as reported by Aftenposten. The four are linked to the sale and storage of about 135 kilos of amphetamine and methamphetamine, about 630 kilos of hashish and marijuana, about 29 kilos of cocaine and more than 200,000 pills. According to the prosecutor, much of the trade took place on the dark web, with payment in cryptocurrency.

item.title: Kryptojätten i ny kontrovers – erbjöd tjänster i Europa utan licens
item.description: EU supervisors are examining Binance for continuing to serve European customers without the licence required under MiCA, Realtid reports, citing the Financial Times. ESMA and national authorities in countries including France, Germany and Greece are looking at how Binance uses the narrow 'reverse solicitation' exemption, which only applies when the customer takes the initiative. Binance says it complies with applicable rules and is working towards a MiCA licence.

item.title: Krypto-jätten rundar reglerna i Europa: Riskerar att kastas ut
item.description: Binance lacks the licence required under the EU's MiCA rules and was supposed to start winding down in the EU from 1 July, yet some European customers are still trading, Dagens PS reports, citing the Financial Times. The exchange relies on the 'reverse solicitation' exemption, which ESMA says must be understood very narrowly. Authorities can request more information and, if they reject Binance's arguments, move to enforcement and fines; Binance says it follows applicable rules.

item.title: Här är riskerna för finansiering av spridning av massförstörelsevapen störst
item.description: Finansinspektionen reports that a new national risk assessment judges the risk of financing the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to be highest in illegal financial activity and through the use of crypto-assets. The assessment comes from the ten authorities in Sweden's Sanctions Coordination Council. It is limited to UN Security Council resolutions with targeted financial sanctions against North Korea or Iran.

item.title: GreenMerc kutter 4,8 millioner i året – Northcrypto går med overskudd
item.description: GreenMerc, the Swedish listed group behind Trijo and Finland's Northcrypto, says it has cut running costs by about SEK 400,000 a month, or around SEK 4.8 million a year, with full effect from October. According to the company, Northcrypto posted a positive operating result in July and August after Trijo's Swedish customers were moved onto its MiCA-licensed platform. The freed-up resources are being directed to Trijo One, a banking offer the company is developing with Marginalen Bank, Kaupr reports.

item.title: Pangstart for nytt kryptofond
item.description: Gersemi Crypto Fund, a new long/short hedge fund run by former top-ranked shipping analyst Joakim Hannisdahl, is up 39 percent since it launched on 5 August, according to Hannisdahl, Finansavisen reports. The fund is driven solely by a mathematical model he keeps secret, which he says showed very high returns in backtesting. Hannisdahl stresses that the strategy is extremely volatile and carries very high risk.

item.title: Yhteisöllisyys ja teknologia kiehtovat kryptovaluuttoihin sijoittaneita – kryptotapahtumassa iloittiin bitcoinin uudesta nousurallista
item.description: About 700 crypto enthusiasts from Finland and abroad attended the Btchel bitcoin event at Kaapelitehdas in Helsinki, where many said community matters more to them than the bitcoin price, Yle reports. The mood was upbeat as bitcoin had risen above USD 86,000 during the week after falling to just over USD 58,000 in the summer. Nordnet told Yle that the typical crypto investor on its platform is a man aged 31 to 50.

item.title: Fant hemmelig passord: Låste opp krypto-lommeboken
item.description: Police have unlocked the crypto wallet of an NHH student in his twenties charged in a drug case, after finding a 12-word recovery phrase during a search of his home, Nettavisen reports, citing Bergensavisen. The police prosecutor says assets worth several hundred thousand kroner have been transferred from the wallet and seized. Hordaland District Court has ruled that the student will stay in custody until the trial starts in mid-November.

item.title: Coinmotion og K33 inngår nordisk kryptosamarbeid om institusjonell handel
item.description: Finnish crypto broker Coinmotion, which serves customers in Finland and Sweden, has chosen K33 as its partner for institutional execution of larger trades, Kaupr reports. Under the deal Coinmotion keeps the customer relationship and platform while K33 carries out the trades, and both firms hold MiCA licences. K33's CEO says MiCA's common framework makes partnerships like this easier.

item.title: Safello åpner for at andre selskaper kan tilby kryptokjøp
item.description: Swedish crypto exchange Safello is piloting a 'crypto checkout' that lets companies without their own crypto business offer crypto purchases inside their services, under Safello's MiCA licence, Kaupr reports. Buyers become Safello customers through its regular know-your-customer checks, and the first test runs in Sweden with one unnamed partner and on Safello-owned bitcoin.se. Safello says it is too early to estimate what the pilot means financially.

item.title: Skal ha stjålet fra egen bedrift – brukte pengene på krypto
item.description: A Norwegian man has been charged with gross embezzlement from his own company and is said to have spent the money on crypto.

item.title: NBX inngår avtale med Tieto om betalingskort for stablecoins
item.description: Norwegian crypto platform NBX has signed an agreement with Tieto Banktech for digital and physical payment cards meant to let customers spend stablecoins without first selling them and moving the money to a bank, Kaupr reports. The programme starts with a prepaid Visa card, with Tieto handling card infrastructure and fraud monitoring and IDT Finance acting as BIN sponsor. NBX's CEO says what sets it apart is that NBX issues its own stablecoins in line with MiCA.

item.title: Minister i nyt skatteopgør: Vil gøre op med »junglen af urimelige og uforståelige regler«
item.description: A review of almost 1,000 cases on how Danes are taxed on crypto-assets found errors in 23 of them, including one person who paid more than DKK 1 million too much in tax, Berlingske reports. Tax and growth minister Jakob Engel-Schmidt reacted on LinkedIn and is promising to clear up what he calls a jungle of unreasonable and incomprehensible rules.

item.title: Danske Bank: Ingen bank kan bygge euro-stablecoin alene
item.description: Speaking at Dansk Blockchain Forum in the Danish parliament, Danske Bank's Mads Clemmensen said no single bank can build a euro stablecoin alone, and that European banks should build an alternative to the dollar together through the Qivalis consortium, Kaupr reports. According to Clemmensen, 99.3 percent of stablecoins are tied to the US dollar, which runs against Europe's aim of depending less on US players. He confirmed that Qivalis plans to launch its euro stablecoin before the end of the year.

item.title: Danskere svindlet for 89 millioner kroner på seks måneder
item.description: Danes lost DKK 89 million to investment fraud in the first half of 2026 across 1,145 registered cases, and crypto played a role in 70.6 percent of them, according to new figures from Finans Danmark reported by Ekstra Bladet. Losses rose 67 percent from the first to the second quarter. Finans Danmark says the scams often start with fake social media ads misusing pictures of well-known Danes, and that some victims are told to lie to their bank.

item.title: 100 år gammel lov koster danske kryptoinvestorer millioner. Nu vil minister problemet til livs
item.description: An answer from Danish tax and growth minister Jakob Engel-Schmidt to a question shows that 325 Danes have paid tax on crypto trading even though they lost money overall, Berlingske reports. The minister called the figure 'actually pretty wild' and wants to change the century-old rule behind it.

item.title: Kollaps for kryptobørs
item.description: Norwegian crypto exchange Firi had revenue of NOK 42 million and costs of NOK 87.5 million in the first half of 2026, giving a net loss of NOK 43.6 million, according to an investor presentation cited by Finansavisen. That compares with a profit of NOK 134.9 million in the record year 2024 and NOK 28 million in 2025. CEO Thuc Tuan Hoang points to weaker trading and extraordinary legal costs for the MiCA licence, and says Firi, which had a NOK 151 million liquidity reserve at the end of June, does not need new capital.

item.title: Slår et slag for stablecoins
item.description: Johanna Belitz, Nordic head of Valour, argues that stablecoins can make money transfers abroad much faster and cheaper, especially to countries outside the EU/EEA with weaker banking infrastructure, Finansavisen reports. By her estimate, a NOK 10,000 bank transfer can easily cost NOK 300–600 in total, against NOK 10–50 with stablecoins. She also points out that stablecoins are not covered by any state deposit guarantee and carry both technical risk and the risk of losing their peg.

item.title: Verdiendringer i bitcoin tynger NBX
item.description: NBX made a pre-tax loss of NOK 21.33 million in the first half of 2026, compared with NOK 9.85 million a year earlier, with much of the loss due to the lower book value of its bitcoin, E24 reports from the company's report. At the same time, NBX converted NOK 19.8 million in loans and interest into 73.5 million new shares. Its bitcoin holdings rose from about 24 at the end of June to 28 in August.

item.title: NBX mer enn doblet tapet i halvåret da MiCA-lisensen kom
item.description: NBX received its MiCA licence in June, but operating revenue fell 45 percent to NOK 6.1 million in the first half of 2026 and the after-tax loss grew to NOK 16.6 million from NOK 7.7 million, Kaupr reports from the half-year report. Platform trading revenue fell sharply, while income from OTC trading and custody almost tripled. Most of the weaker result came from a fall in the value of its bitcoin holdings, which the company describes as an unrealised loss.

item.title: Regjeringen utreder midlertidig forbud mot nye kryptodatasentre (skriftlig spørsmål 15:3707)
item.description: In a written question to the minister of digitalisation and public administration, Sofie Marhaug (Red Party) asks when the government will present its announced state planning provision to limit crypto mining. She also asks which EEA provisions and legal assessments underlie the government's conclusion that Norway cannot introduce a general mining ban, noting that the Storting has asked the government three times in two years to work on a ban. Minister Torgeir Micaelsen answered the question on 18 September.
